## SECTION 0. ANALYSIS OVERVIEW & BUSINESS CLASSIFICATION

**Layer 0-1. Enterprise Archetype: D — Product-Platform Hybrid with transition signals toward B — Quality Compounder** [selected by analyst]

*Reasons for Archetype D:*
1. Revenue is 50%+ hardware/semiconductor (custom AI XPUs, networking, broadband ASICs) but is bundled with long-duration engineering co-development relationships (Google, Meta, OpenAI, ByteDance, Fujitsu — TechTimes, Sep 2026 [Estimate]).
2. Infrastructure Software (VMware, mainframe, storage/network software) is a high-margin recurring platform (~90% gross margin; AlphaSense [Estimate]) and is 40%+ of revenue.
3. AI XPU engagements are multi-year platform-like lock-ins (each is an engineering co-development, not a transactional chip sale — TechTimes [Actual — mgmt commentary]).

**Layer 0-2. Valuation Engine Selected: Engine 3 (Hybrid — Core + Platform), cross-checked by Engine 4 (Expectation-Driven Reverse DCF), because the equity value is dominated by multi-year AI-revenue expectations that outrun any "core" franchise DCF anchor.**

**Layer 0-3. Transition logic** — The AI semiconductor ramp, if delivered at the scale guided ($115B FY27), would push AVGO closer to B (Quality Compounder), but ROIC > WACC for 3 consecutive cycles is not yet established, and the NVIDIA-dominated merchant segment plus hyperscaler captive design (TPU/MTIA) keeps this a **cyclical-option hybrid — not a terminal Quality Compounder**. Full archetype upgrade requires margin volatility to fall and ROIC > WACC for 3 more years.

**Layer 0-4. Engine selection rationale & errors avoided** — Using only a steady-state full-company DCF would undervalue the near-term AI orders; using a pure E (option) engine would overstate precision on a company with $100B+ near-term revenue and $30B+ cash flow. A hybrid best captures both.
